mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in UNRATE above 4.1% by more than 0.3 percentage points within three months triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rise does not exceed 0.3pp in 3 months, or 20-day returns are not positive when triggered.

mechanism_narrative: Both demand (GDPC1) and supply (INDPRO) indices rising above their respective 3-month moving averages simultaneously predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days during an expansionary phase.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and INDPRO above 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: The combined GDPC1 and INDPRO signal does not predict positive returns in expansionary phases (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate and increase in demand (GDPC1) both over three months predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during expansionary policy.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS decline AND GDPC1 increase over 3 months
failure_condition: The combined FEDFUNDS decline and GDPC1 increase do not correlate with positive returns in expansionary periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPIAUCSL inflation index predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days under conditions of rising inflationary pressure.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rise does not lead to negative returns in inflationary periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in employment (PAYEMS) exceeding 50,000 workers triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days during a labor market surge.
failure_condition: PAYEMS spike does not result in positive 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate during a late-cycle expansion predicts higher positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days compared to baseline conditions.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, FEDFUNDS decline does not produce higher returns than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Both demand (GDPC1) and labor demand (PAYEMS) indices rising above their 3-month moving averages simultaneously predict positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days during expansionary labor demand.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and PAYEMS above 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: The combined GDPC1 and PAYEMS signal does not predict positive returns in expansionary labor demand (p > 0.05).
